messages:
zuo: FYI bringing up boreal-64k-int4 on staging. Hit a weird longprefill artifact where tokens from much earlier in the prompt reappear after a shard-merge event. Minimal logs below. Anyone seen a shard-merge/rebase flip before?

emily: can you paste the repro and compile/runtime flags?

zuo: repro (single-line):
```bash
./bin/serve_onboard --model=boreal-64k-int4 --prompt=tests/long/40k.md \
  --quant=int4v3 --kv-mode=sharded --kv-merge-policy=auto --rope_scale=dynamic
```
logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-04-02T21:07:01Z] kv: shard_merge initiated src_shard=11 dst_shard=5 merge_seq_base=41200
[2026-04-02T21:07:01Z] kv: rebase applied dst_shard=5 old_seq_base=40000 new_seq_base=41200
[2026-04-02T21:07:01Z] prefill: wrote shard=11 seq_base=41200 len=512 fp=0x4f2a8c9b
[2026-04-02T21:07:02Z] decode: reading shard=5 seq=41200 fp=0x4f2a8c9a
[2026-04-02T21:07:02Z] token_dup: token[37012]==token[14512]
```

nav: fp LSB off by 1 (0x...9b vs 0x...9a) and merge/rebase immediately before replay. Could be a half-write during async merge or a packing alignment bug where int4 nibble flip occurs on a boundary.

harper: interesting: int4v3 uses a custom packer with 64-bit store ops. If merge copies slices that aren't 8-aligned you can get a stale nibble. Did the merge happen during an in-flight prefill?

zuo: yes, logs show prefill and merge overlapped by ~150ms. We have async merge enabled to reduce tail latencies. I re-ran with kv-merge-policy=serial and the repro disappeared. Also re-run with quant=int8 -> no repro.

emily: hypothesis: the async merge path is doing unprotected memcpy of packed buffers; concurrent writer can leave a partially-updated 64-bit word and reader sees an inconsistent nibble. For int8 it never packs that way so it's safe. Two fixes: 1) make merge atomic wrt packed-word writes (use per-word CAS or copy into scratch aligned buffer then publish), 2) add a strict pre/post-merge quiesce so prefill waits for outstanding merges.

nav: short-term mitigation: disable async shard_merge for int4 onboard builds; long-term: make the packer produce word-aligned writes or switch merges to RCU publish pattern. I'll sketch a patch.

zuo: filed internal ticket: KV-MERGE-PARTIALWRITE-31277 with repro and heap dumps. https://redwood.internal/issue/KV-MERGE-PARTIALWRITE-31277

ci-bot: CI job queued: CI/kv-packer#31277 (staging). Will post when finished. :gear:

harper: also saw a subtle RoPE jitter: dynamic rope_scale differs slightly after merge in the live decode path (rope_scale=1.0000 at write, 0.99985 at read). Even tiny scale deltas + nibble corruption = reproducible token shifts. We should snapshot rope_scale into shard metadata at merge and prefer header on replay.

emily: agree. Plan: A) revert async shard_merge for int4 canaries, B) enforce atomic publish for packed buffers (patch in kv/pack.cc), C) snapshot rope_scale into shard header on write/merge, D) add unit test that simulates concurrent packer writes and verifies no partial-word exposure.

zuo: implemented short-term config change and re-ran the 40k prompt for 6h soak: no artifact observed. Keeping this canary up for 24h before unblocking onboarding.

nav: I'll open PR: fix/kv-atomic-merge-31277 with a microbenchmark and unit tests. Tagging harper for rope header change.

emily: :thumbsup: Add a regression in ci/longprefill matrix for int4v3 + async-merge on/off so we catch this in presubmit.

ci-bot: Patch CI started: ci/kv-packer#31277. Results will follow. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
